Hi everyone!
I’ve formalized Green's relations for semigroups in Lean 4, mostly following section 2.3 of Thomas Colcombet's paper, "The Factorisation Forest Theorem".
My ultimate goal is Simon's Factorisation Forest Theorem.
The Simon proof itself is still a messy work in progress, but the Green's relations implementation is stable, compiles without any sorry, and is ready for review.
You can find the repo here: https://github.com/ReemMelamed/greenFFT.git
Does this look like a good fit for mathlib?
If so, I plan to break it down into a few small PRs.
I’ll probably start with adding the basic definitions.
I’d love to hear your thoughts or any advice on how to proceed :)

I've opened PR #40050 adding basic definitions for Green's relations.
CI is passing, and I'd appreciate a review when convenient.

Why did you request a review from Copilot :sob:

Either way, this PR seems to contain only definitions and no theorems ( which your first post stated, but in lieu of feedback then) . Not withstanding accuracy/relevance, you want a much healthier ratio of definitions : results if you can.

I hope this doesn't mean copilot review is unwelcome in mathlib in general? I often use it to catch trivial typos

Haha sorry, the Copilot request must've been an accident.
I probably misclicked somewhere in the PR process. I'll remove it.

Thanks for the feedback on the ratio.
My thought process was to keep the first PR as minimal as possible, but you're right, thanks for pointing that out.
As you can see in my repo, I already have a lot of properties of Green's relations formalized.
I'll push the basic ones to this PR today so it has a much healthier ratio.
I see no issue with requesting a review from copilot. In fact, we might have more LLM-powered reviewing in the not so far future

Just a quick update: I've pushed changes to PR #40050 based on the feedback of @Yan Yablonovskiy 🇺🇦.
I added Basic.lean, which contains the basic properties of Green's relations.
I'd appreciate a review when convenient. Thanks!

Is there a reason you opted not to do abbrev IsGreenJRel (a b : S) := (a = b) ∨ (∃ z, a = z * b ∨ a = b * z) ∨ ∃ u v, a = u * b * v ? I also think perhaps you should avoid so much idiosyncratic naming, usually in Mathlib things are rarely named after a person.

I left a tiny bit of an initial review.

Yan Yablonovskiy 🇺🇦 said:

Is there a reason you opted not to do abbrev IsGreenJRel (a b : S) := (a = b) ∨ (∃ z, a = z * b ∨ a = b * z) ∨ ∃ u v, a = u * b * v ? I also think perhaps you should avoid so much idiosyncratic naming, usually in Mathlib things are rarely named after a person.

I left a tiny bit of an initial review.

Thanks for the review!
Your suggestion for the IsGreenJRel.trans proof is great and I applied it.

I used "Green" as I didn't want to clash with any definition that is already in mathlib.
What would you recommend doing here?

About IsGreenJRel, initially I used an abbrev, but when I tried to prove its properties it got quite messy.
So for me, a custom inductive with named constructors was easier to manage.

Hello, I have also been working on formalizing Green's relations with a small team of people from Boston College, and we have a github repo that seems to formalize many similar theorems as yours. Here is a link: https://github.com/lean-summer-research/Updated

We were focusing on the Rees-Suschkewitch theorem rather than Simon's Factorization Forest Theorem, but it seems to me like we proved a lot of similar results along the way.

We are just beginning to submit PRs for this work, and I made a PR #40241 that has some fundamental results about idempotent powers of elements in finite semigroups.

I would be very interested in expanding on this work if your PR is merged.

One suggestion I have for now is to provide infix notation for Green's relations, which resembles the notation used in the textbooks we have been basing our work around (mostly two books by Jean-Eric Pin, ‘Varieties of Formal Languages’, and ‘Mathematical Foundations of Automata Theory’). For example, you could write 'x 𝓙 y rather than IsGreenJ x y`.
